Hi Lena —

Thanks for the PO and the clear asks. We can absolutely do a single consolidated PDF invoice that contains two invoiced lines, each with its own remit instructions and tax ID. Quick summary of what we need from you to generate it cleanly: 

1) For each legal entity you want funds routed to, please confirm:
   - Legal entity name exactly as it should appear on the invoice (e.g., "Atlas Health Inc.")
   - VAT / Tax ID
   - Preferred remit destination ("bank transfer to GL 4001" or "AP portal remittance to ap@...")
   - Billing contact/email for remittance questions

2) Which allocation rule should we apply to split the PO total? Options:
   A) Percentage split (e.g., 60/40) — simplest for recurring seats
   B) Seat-level mapping (you provide CSV with seat->entity) — recommended if allocation varies by seat
   C) One-off line-level amounts you want billed now (we'll honor line amounts)

I've attached a small CSV template "split_template.csv" you can use to list entity mapping (seat_id, amount, remit_to, tax_id). If you prefer to send back a signed amendment instead, we can do that too; this is more of an ops preference.

Marissa (cc'd) — could you please prepare a draft invoice once we have the two tax IDs and allocation rule? Ben, I know you own the multi-entity invoice flow — can you confirm current limitations around showing per-line remit instructions in our consolidated PDF?

Lena — once we have the above we can turn around a draft invoice same day (for US bank transfers). If there are international wires or FTAs that require different references, we'll include those fields as text under each line.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: split_template.csv (text/csv)
